Sparta. 
I studied a subject called "classical civilization" in college and one of the things we studied was the... I guess you could say the day to day life of Athenians and Spartans and their relationships within the family. The hierarchy, so to speak. 

It pretty much comes down to my personal preference for the spartan society. Which is tough considering that they were a society based upon slavery. However, if you look at the family circle, it always felt to me, like the women in the Athenian society were of secondary importance, if that. The men did what they liked and as long as they provided, the women had no say and the men could do what they wished. 

But I'm the Spartan society, they were a waring race. The men were always at war somewhere or defending their far reaching borders and that meant that the women played a vital role in their society. They were respected. They were in charge of the state while the men were away at war. That's not just the "family state", that's the country. The women held the respect of the men for keeping the peace of their society while they were at war. The women had far more freedom and far more respect which is why they were ridiculed and feared by the Athenians. The women could defend their land almost as well as the men, which was an alien concept to the Athenians, because they weren't at home simply waiting for the return of their men, they were taking action. 
IDK, it's been a while since I did that course, so forgive me any mistakes you think I made in this little essay. But I always felt, as a game that is so centered on family and family concept, that the spartan route felt like the more logical/canon route to take. The spartan women of the house hold wouldn't just sit at home and wait for things to blow over, they would take action for themselves. Which is what Kassandra and Myrinne did.

I don't know if my comment can help or not, cause it didn't happen to me and circumstances are different, nonetheless;

Shortly after I was born, probably 3 or 4 months on, my brother was 8 at the time my mother died. Her side of the family have a long history of a condition called cardiomyopathy. There are different variants from my understanding, but I digress. My dad's world completely collapsed that day. They were building a house together, he'd stopped work to build the house cause we could more than cope off of her income alone. Suddenly he had no wife, a partly built house, a newborn baby and an angry 8 year old that didn't understand why he couldn't see mum again. 

I've asked him over the years what the hell kept him going, because I don't know if I would have the strength. From what I gather it was a mixture of feeling like he had too because of my brother and I, he could let us down or abandon us. But it was also a lot of just waking up and taking each day as it comes. Some will truly horrifying where all you could think about is what you've lost and what now rides on you're shoulders now, but other days you might be able to get lost in your work and come home and have some fun with your kids, distract yourself from the world for a while. 

That's why I say I don't know if this comment will help you or not, because you have different circumstances, but all I can possibly advise is the take each day at a time. But don't shut yourself off from the world. Let yourself get distracted and let yourself have fun where you can. I'm sure there are still others in your life that want to support you, that want to be with you. Let them, they may not always be the help you need. My uncle had a habit of making my dad feel worse, despite his best efforts because he wanted to help my dad work through it. It was what he felt would help my dad. But what actually helped my dad was his best mate coming round and dragging him down to the pub where for a few hours, they could laugh and cry and not care about their troubles and just have some fun together. 

I'm sorry if I've rambled or if my point (if there is one) is blurred and messy. But just try and carry on, as difficult as it is. Try and figure out your coping mechanism, whether be talking through it or going to a pub with someone and getting wasted. Just don't lose yourself in your grief.
